html:
The Maracanazo was the deciding match of the 1950 World Cup, played at the Maracanã stadium in Rio de Janeiro on 16 July 1950. Uruguay beat Brazil 2-1 before a crowd of about 200,000.

Brazil needed only a draw, and newspapers had already declared it champion. Brazil scored first, but Uruguay, led by its captain Obdulio Varela, equalised, and Alcides Ghiggia scored the winner late in the game. The stadium fell silent.

For Uruguay, a nation of about two million, it was a second world title after the first World Cup of 1930, and it became a national myth. In Brazil it was remembered as a national tragedy, and the team changed its white shirts for the yellow it has worn since.
sum: The Maracanazo was the deciding match of the 1950 World Cup, played at the Maracanã stadium in Rio de Janeiro on 16 July 1950. Uruguay beat Brazil 2-1 before a crowd of about 200,000.
